absent: Exact bit layout and numeric values for migration flags, fault codes, allocation masks, page orders, masks and counts.
Internals of content movement, migration entry installation and removal, reverse mapping updates and TLB batching architecture effects.
Folio and page table lock implementations, full ordering rules and deadlock avoidance beyond what unmap preparation shows.
Deferred split queue mechanics, partially mapped tracking and reclaim list drain behavior.
Memory control group charging, swap throttling, collapse daemon interaction and event accounting semantics.
User fault interception, stable address space validation, out of memory handling and special mapping behavior.
Huge zero folio shrinker reclamation, per address space flag management and frame number use.
Splitter internals for reducing large folios, retry limit policies and statistics structure layout.
File system private buffer release, movable operation callbacks and migration cause tagging.

findings.text: Public helper that reduces a large folio to smallest order pages and attaches results to a caller supplied list, delegating the actual split to the huge page splitter.
Public per task helper that completes any pending batched unmap TLB work and clears the pending and writable marks when no flush is required it does nothing.
Public accessor for the shared huge zero folio, offered in alternate builds where one returns the global directly and another manages per address space membership with reference counting.
Public helper that prepares deferred split accounting for a folio, succeeding immediately when memory control groups are disabled and otherwise allocating list state for the deferred split queue.
Public helper that chooses an allocation and reclaim style for transparent huge pages from global defragmentation policy combined with whether the area carries a huge page advice.

Public installer for an anonymous transparent huge page mapping that builds a page middle directory entry with area protections, adds exclusive reverse mapping and least recently used membership, publishes the entry, refreshes the cache and queues deferred split.

Anonymous transparent huge page fault entry that validates suitability and preparation, registers with the collapse daemon, then either installs the shared zero folio for read faults where allowed or delegates to the allocating fault path.

Batch migration orchestration entry that first attempts asynchronous batch migration and then falls back to single folio synchronous attempts, merging statistics and directing unmigrated folios to retention or input lists according to outcome.

Unmap preparation obtains a destination through a caller callback and fails for lack of memory when none is supplied, then applies mode specific blocking rules where asynchronous work never waits, light synchronous work avoids waiting on non current or under writeback pages, full synchronous work waits for writeback, and direct compaction context never takes a blocking lock.

Anonymous non shared kernel same page folios pin their anonymous map structure across unmapping so the structure cannot be released while the mapping count temporarily drops, with the pin released on both success and undo paths.

Destination folios carry interim migration state in a single word that combines the pinned anonymous map pointer with flags for prior locked and mapped status, written on successful unmap and cleared on extraction before movement or undo.
Folios carrying movable operations bypass normal unmapping and content movement, recording prior state during unmap and delegating movement to the per page movable operation during the move phase.

Unmapping distinguishes absent mappings with private buffers which attempt buffer release and fail, mapped folios which install migration entries and remember mapped status, and already unmapped folios which proceed directly to recording.

Undo helpers restore migration entries when the source had been mapped, drop any anonymous map pin, release held locks, return the source to the caller retention list when retry is not requested, and release the destination through a caller callback or reference drop.

Splitting attempt locks according to migration mode with nonblocking attempt for asynchronous work and blocking lock otherwise, delegates to the folio splitter, unlocks, and queues the folio with split results only on success.

Batch movement walks source and destination lists in lockstep, cooperatively reschedules, invokes single folio movement, and classifies outcomes as freed on success, retained for retry on transient failure, or counted as failed with page and huge page accounting otherwise.

Successful single folio movement preserves deferred split queue membership, moves contents to the destination, requeues the destination when needed, adds the destination to the reclaim list before removing migration entries so locked accounting is correct, drains the reclaim addition when previously locked, then releases references and frees the source while tagging the destination with the migration cause.

Transient failure preserves pairing for a later attempt by relinking the destination at its prior position and rewriting saved state, while other failures invoke full undo of both source and destination.
Batch undo walks paired lists together, extracts saved state per destination, undoes each source with correct mapped flag and retention list, unlinks each destination and releases it.

Synchronous migration first attempts an asynchronous batch with bounded retries and merges partial statistics, then on non fatal outcome returns remaining work to the input list and retries folios singly in the requested mode with bounded synchronous retries, accumulating failure counts without double counting split huge pages.
Fault allocation mask derives from the file mapping with filesystem and input output allowances when a file is present, and falls back to a default kernel mask for special mappings without a file.

Huge page middle directory fault dispatch sends anonymous areas to the anonymous huge fault path, file areas with huge fault operations to that operation at page middle directory order, and all other cases to the small page fallback.

Anonymous huge read faults may install the shared zero folio when the address space allows zero pages and global policy enables the huge zero page, requiring allocation of a page table, acquisition of the zero folio, and validation under lock that the entry remains empty with stable address space and no user fault interception before installation.

Huge zero folio management uses a fast reference increment when already alive, otherwise allocates once under lock with an extra pin for the shrinker, shares a single global folio and frame number, and treats final release by anyone other than the shrinker as a warning.
Zero folio allocation requests a zeroed transparent huge order folio without movable placement and explicitly marks it as not large mappable, counting allocation failure as an event.

Allocating anonymous huge fault path allocates a folio and page table, validates under lock that the entry is still empty with stable address space, diverts to user fault handling with full cleanup when interception applies, otherwise deposits the table, maps the folio, accounts page tables and succeeds, freeing resources with out of memory or fallback status on failure.

Anonymous huge folio allocation for a faulting aligned address obtains a folio, charges the memory control group, prepares deferred accounting, throttles swap activity, zeroes for user when required, and marks current with ordering that makes zeroing visible before publication, releasing the folio and counting fallback on any failure.

Allocation policy for transparent huge pages selects among always synchronous compaction, background reclaim with quick failure, mixed choice based on advice, advice only synchronous compaction, or light background reclaim, driven by global defragmentation flags.
Counting variant of anonymous huge mapping installation additionally accounts anonymous pages and allocation events for virtual memory, multi size huge page and control group statistics.

Source folio lock is held from unmap preparation through movement completion or undo, destination folio lock is acquired nonblockingly during unmap and held through movement or undo, with both released on success with destination before source and individually in undo helpers only when actually held.

Page middle directory lock serializes emptiness checks and huge mapping installation including zero folio installation, while the dedicated huge zero lock serializes one time installation of the shared zero folio and frame number.

Anonymous map pin acts as a lifetime guard rather than a mutual exclusion lock, held from unmap through move or undo to prevent release while reverse mapping count is zero, paired with folio locks that prevent remapping during the window.

Folio split attempt holds the folio lock across the split operation only, using nonblocking acquisition for asynchronous migration and blocking acquisition otherwise, always releasing before returning.

Destination folio interim field packs a pointer to the pinned anonymous map structure together with low flag bits for prior locked and mapped status, with masking used to separate pointer from flags and clearing after extraction.

Source and destination folio lists use least recently used linkage with positional pairing where each source entry corresponds to the destination entry at the same position, manipulated by unlinking the destination before movement and relinking on retry.
Current task unmap batch state carries a flush required flag, a writable flag and architecture specific batch data, where flush clears both flags after issuing the architecture flush.

Fault handling context links a virtual area with its file, flags, protections and address space to a fault address and page middle directory location plus lock slot and fault flags that distinguish read from write.

Folio migration proceeds through destination acquisition, source locking, writeback disposition, anonymous pinning, destination locking, unmapping with migration entries, state recording, content movement, reclaim list insertion, migration entry removal and dual unlock with source freeing, with exits to retry preservation or full undo at each failure.

Anonymous huge fault proceeds through suitability and preparation, collapse daemon registration, zero versus allocating branch selection, table and folio acquisition, locked validation of emptiness and stability and user interception, then installation or fallback or out of memory or user fault diversion.

Shared huge zero folio lifecycle moves from absent to allocating to installed with shrinker pin, then shared by additional references with per address space membership tracking, with release paths that never reach zero except through the shrinker.

Blocking on a folio lock from direct compaction context risks double locking the same page when readahead merges multiple pages for one input output, so unmap preparation fails fast instead of waiting in that context.

Dropping reverse mapping count to zero during migration would allow the anonymous map structure to be freed unnoticed, so failure to pin it is only safe when the page is already unmapped and locked against remap.

Invoking unmapping against a folio without a mapping triggers a fatal check, so absent mappings are handled separately with buffer release rather than entering the unmap path, and orphaned pages with filesystem private state cannot migrate until that state is freed.
Destination folio may still be in prior use when migration acquires it, so failure of its nonblocking lock is treated as ordinary failure rather than a fatal error.
Movable operation migration requires both movable operations and prior isolation, warns when either precondition is missing, and only clears isolation on success.
Decrementing the huge zero reference count to zero outside the shrinker indicates a lifetime bug and raises a one time warning.

Page middle directory may become populated between fault entry and lock acquisition or lose address space stability, so locked revalidation must precede installation and any user fault interception must release all acquired resources before diversion.

Migration modes distinguish asynchronous nonblocking, light synchronous with limited waiting, and full synchronous with writeback waiting, governing lock acquisition, writeback and unmap batching choices.
Migration outcome codes distinguish lack of memory, transient retry, busy writeback and generic failure, where transient retry retains list pairing and other outcomes restore or count failure.
Saved migration flags distinguish prior locked and prior mapped status and their combination mask for separating flags from the packed anonymous map pointer.
Fault result codes distinguish fallback to small pages and out of memory during huge fault handling, with fallback also used when suitability, zero acquisition, allocation or charging fails.
Huge page geometry facts link page middle directory order with aligned mask, huge order and page count used for allocation size, address alignment and accounting.

Allocation and advice facts link transparent huge and light variants with movable, zeroing, retry, direct reclaim and background reclaim modifiers plus huge page advice and global defragmentation policy flags.
Fault and mapping flags distinguish write faults from read faults, anonymous areas from file areas, and direct compaction allocation context from normal context.
